description: Faryab protest start is reported as Jan. 13 by several accounts; one Jan. 16 account’s “four days ago” implies Jan. 12. No exact clock/time sequence resolves it.
required_followup: New Dari sources Etilaatroz and DW both give Jan. 13, while Hasht’s “four days ago” relative to Jan. 16 still implies Jan. 12. Compare original timeline and preserve the conflict if unresolved.

description: Faryab public protest is entangled in reporting with factional armed takeover/clashes. It is not clear which actions were by demonstrators, residents, or armed Taliban factions.
required_followup: Separate the public assembly from armed events if primary evidence allows; keep conflicting actors distinct.

description: Faryab physical ending and any transition from protest to armed confrontation remain unclear. DW also reports a Jan. 14 call to resume protest at Eidgah Mosque followed by Taliban dispersal, without establishing whether this was a new gathering or continuation of the Jan. 13 protest.
required_followup: Establish physical close and sequence; distinguish the Jan. 13 street/tent protest from any Jan. 14 Eidgah attempted restart without inferring continuity or event end.

description: Turnout for the Jan. 9, Jan. 11, Jan. 13, and Jan. 22 women’s demonstrations is not reported in reviewed sources.
required_followup: Find event-specific contemporary accounts; do not infer >=50 from multiple actions or a campaign total.

description: Jan. 12 Kabul report says “dozens,” which does not resolve whether participation reached 50.
required_followup: Seek exact count or additional event-specific contemporary evidence.

description: Jan. 9 Kabul protest followed an academic’s arrest, but the reviewed chronology does not state a specific demand or target.
required_followup: Find a source stating the protest’s expressed demand and intended target.

description: Jan. 11 VOA and CIR chronology plausibly refer to the same action; exact equivalence and independence are not established.
required_followup: Compare dates, images, quoted participants and sequence in any additional available reports.

description: Several Faryab articles may relay local/agency reporting with overlapping accounts. Independent provenance and exact syndication links require further review. Etilaatroz credits itself and DW cites local freelance reporter Qutbuddin Kohi, but overlap among local-source accounts is not fully resolved.
required_followup: Record explicit original-source links/bylines before counting corroboration.

description: Several accounts conflate the protest with armed factional conflict. DW additionally reports guard fire according to protesters, one Taliban public-order officer killed, four protesters injured, and a Jan. 14 dispersal, but the full action/actor sequence and the separate event relation remain unresolved; do not code protester violence or armed casualty transfer from “clashes” alone.
required_followup: Coordinator review of the cited passage and manual state-response definitions; resolve actor, timing, target and whether the Jan. 14 dispersal is event-linked before assigning any response dimensions.

description: Jan. 11 VOA says Taliban fighters later stopped protesters, but the sequence and whether this was formal crowd dispersal need review.
required_followup: Compare with codebook response definitions and seek more detail; keep unknown if not established.

description: The Jan. 19 home raids are broadly associated with recent women’s activism, but a specific response relationship to any single public gathering is not established.
required_followup: Trace each victim/organizer/event link; do not attribute raids to a specific protest absent direct evidence.

description: UNAMA Pashto June 2022 report URL returned HTTP 403 on an ordinary access attempt; retain the barrier and do not retry the origin.
required_followup: Use other already-available sources; no bypass or same-origin alternate.

description: Pashto ACLED/APW PDF was read only partially from ordinary public request; extracted scope includes women’s protest context and Faryab conflict but not a complete page-by-page reading.
required_followup: Only resume within permitted ordinary public retrieval if needed; preserve the existing partial scope.

description: Open-web review is non-exhaustive and does not reproduce LexisNexis access; lack of a result is not evidence that no event occurred.
required_followup: Continue targeted regional, sector, local-language and retrospective searches; note unavailable archive access.

description: January public mobilizations outside the already identified Kabul women’s actions and Faryab remain undercovered; regional and sector coverage needs continuation.
required_followup: Continue province-specific/local-language and labor, education, price, land and political-process searches.

description: Dari/Persian and Pashto discovery was conducted, but local-media coverage and variant spellings/transliteration remain incomplete.
required_followup: Continue local-language regional searches and verify discovered reporting in accessible primary/contemporary sources.

description: The EASO country report is useful pre-period context but explicitly stops at 8 Dec. 2021, with only a Dec. 26 policy note. No continuous Dec-to-Jan episode is established by it; coverage for December events and February follow-up remains incomplete.
required_followup: Search specifically for Dec. 2021 actions with documented continuation into January and for January actions continuing in February; do not transfer the EASO report’s 2021 examples absent same-episode evidence.

description: The official A/HRC report PDF and UNAMA Pashto report URLs returned HTTP 403 and were not read. EUAA’s August 2022 report has now been opened selectively, but its contemporary TOLO/Khaama references have not been directly read.
required_followup: Respect both saved 403 barriers and do not retry those origins. For any other exact public URL, conduct fresh access checks and manual review before retrieval; preserve indirect citation limits.

description: The 24 Jan. Daykundi indoor women-activist action has no attendance count; the report gives no evidence that it reached 50.
required_followup: Seek an event-specific source with an attendance estimate; do not infer turnout from the plural “women activists”.

description: The 24 Jan. Daykundi report quotes demands for proper humanitarian-aid management and monitoring but does not identify a responsible domestic government actor or establish that the indoor meeting was a public gathering.
required_followup: Clarify the gathering’s public-access status and whether the demand was directed to Afghan authorities or aid organizations; leave demands unclassified until target/policy linkage is evidenced.

description: EUAA names a January Kabul rally over two women’s violent deaths and cites a Jan. 16 TOLO article, but exact date and identity are unresolved; the rally could be the Jan. 16 demonstration already excluded for reported attendance of about 20–25.
required_followup: Do not merge or split without direct comparison; preserve the excluded event’s observed counts, and seek accessible contemporaneous evidence for exact date, identity and turnout. The TOLO URL is not to be retried under the existing blocked-origin restriction.

description: The contemporary Khaama article cited by EUAA for a 26 Jan. frozen-funds protest returned a web-viewer Cache miss and HTTP 403 on one ordinary exact-URL request. A fresh check later returned hold; no retry or alternate-host retrieval was made.
required_followup: Respect the exact-URL hold. Use only already available independent evidence; do not retrieve a syndicated/alternate copy of this same report as a bypass.

description: The indirect Jan. 26 frozen-assets protest lead does not establish the precise event location linkage, attendance, publicness, or whether demands targeted Afghanistan’s government or foreign authorities.
required_followup: Keep pending evidence. Resolve exact event linkage and target only through material that does not bypass the held source; do not infer attendance or state target from discovery snippets.

description: DW says supporters called residents to Eidgah Mosque on Fri. 14 Jan. to restart protests but Taliban forces dispersed them. The report does not provide attendance or settle whether an assembly formed, or whether it was a new event, attempted continuation, or part of the Jan. 13 protest sequence.
required_followup: Keep separate from the Jan. 13 event until public gathering, turnout and episode relationship are established; do not infer a new ≥50 action or extend the Jan. 13 end date.
